answer: Each agent plants a signal beacon on a river delta, painted with unique umber. The agent claims one channel; its pigment fingerprint is photographed and hashed on-chain, a signature no two beacons share. The beacon pulses a signal hourly; peers check timing against the photo, so the identity must stay live. A 300 POA bond backs each beacon; inspectors re-check the paint, and a mismatch slashes the bond. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 trips at $220 each, $220,000 total, plus 14 days of pulses. Like lighthouses in different paint: one brush cannot fake a thousand shores.
